Estimate sleep with the AcceleRest model

Source: R/acti_sleep_rester.R
acti_rester.Rd

Runs rester::estimate_rest(), the AcceleRest model of Lorenzen et al. (2026), on raw triaxial acceleration and converts its sleep-stage predictions to the common acti_sleep_estimate format. AcceleRest predicts deep, light, REM, and wake stages for 30-second epochs over context windows of about 2.1 hours, so at least that much data is needed.

Usage

acti_rester(
  data,
  model = c("lstm_sleepstages", "linear_sleepstages"),
  sample_rate = NULL,
  tz = NULL,
  cache_dir = rester::ar_cache_dir(),
  context_window_shift = 1L,
  max_batch_size = 16L,
  device = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing timestamps and triaxial acceleration, or a readable accelerometry file path (a device file or CSV; .h5 files are not supported because they have no time stamps). File paths are passed unchanged to rester::estimate_rest().

model

The sleep-stage head to use: "lstm_sleepstages" (default) or "linear_sleepstages".

sample_rate

Sample rate (Hz) of the input. If NULL, it is found with actibase::get_sample_rate() (from the sample_rate attribute, the header, or the time stamps).

tz

Time zone of the returned times. By default the time zone of data$time, or the time zone of the times read from a file.

For data-frame input, the clock passed to rester is held at the UTC offset in effect at the start of the recording, as actipy works on clock times without a time zone. The returned times are the exact instants of the input, shown in tz.

cache_dir

Directory with the downloaded AcceleRest code and weights; see rester::ar_setup().

context_window_shift

Number of 30-second epochs to shift consecutive context windows; see rester::estimate_rest().

max_batch_size

Number of context windows per forward pass.

device

torch device, e.g. "cpu", "cuda", or "mps". If NULL, rester chooses.

...

Additional arguments passed to rester::ar_read(), such as fill_zeros, detect_nonwear, or verbose.

Value

An acti_sleep_estimate tibble with time, sleep, sleep_probability, sleep_stage, nonwear, and method. sleep_probability is one minus the probability of wake, sleep_stage is the most probable of "deep", "light", "rem", and "wake", and epochs with no valid data have NA for sleep, sleep_probability, sleep_stage, and nonwear. The actipy information about the data is in attr(x, "info").

Details

The model code and weights must be downloaded first with rester::ar_setup().

References

Lorenzen NR, Brink-Kjaer A, Jennum PJ, Mignot E (2026). AcceleRest: A Physiology-Aware Masked Autoencoder for Wrist Accelerometer-based Sleep Staging and Apnea Evaluation. medRxiv. doi:10.64898/2026.01.28.26345056

Examples

# \donttest{
  # Runs only after rester::ar_setup(), so Python is not set up otherwise
  if (rester::ar_have_repo() &&
      rester::ar_have_weights("lstm_sleepstages") &&
      rester::ar_python_modules_installed()) {
    data <- rester::ar_example_data(n_hours = 2.5)
    out <- acti_rester(data, context_window_shift = 32L)
    head(out)
  }
# }
